## What happens when the ratio is 1? {#ss6-ratio-one .gs-lesson .gs-ratio-one}

If $r=1$, every term equals $a$.

$$a,\ a,\ a,\ \ldots,\ a$$

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}

The usual formula would give

$$\frac{a(1-1^n)}{1-1}=\frac00,$$

which is undefined.

:::


::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}

Add $n$ equal terms directly:

$$S_n=\underbrace{a+a+\cdots+a}_{n\text{ terms}}=na.$$

:::


<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 40 · Special case</p>

::: notes


Ask students why r=1 was excluded. First click exposes the undefined quotient. The original finite sum still exists. Second click finds it directly as na. This is not assigning a value to 0/0. Every non-zero constant sequence is both an AP with d=0 and a GP with r=1. The class uses non-zero terms for its ratio-test convention.

:::
